steps: Start the local stack; sign in as the seeded test user.
POST /api/upload with a generated 1×1 PNG (stand-in for an ID photo).
GET the returned URL with no cookies or Authorization header → 200 image/png.
title: Identity documents and selfies are stored at public, non-expiring URLs
standards: Ethiopia Proclamation 1321/2024 (security of processing) — confirm article with counsel
expected: Verification selfies and ID documents are stored privately and readable only by the owner and authorised reviewers, through short-lived signed URLs — as payment receipts already are (backend/lib/privateReceipts.ts).
actual: Verification uses the general uploadFile() → POST /api/upload path. Files are served without authentication: locally via express.static at /uploads, in production via a Supabase bucket the server creates with public: true and /storage/v1/object/public/ URLs. Object names are Date.now() plus Math.random()*1e9 (about 30 bits, not cryptographic) and never expire. The URLs are stored in verification_requests and shown to admins.
impact: Anyone who obtains a URL (admin screen sharing, logs, browser history, a leaked export, a CDN or proxy cache) gets permanent unauthenticated access to a person's government ID and face. Assumption for CVSS: the attacker must first learn or derive the URL (AT:P).
fix: Add a private upload kind for verification (and any other sensitive documents): store in a private bucket under a key with 128+ bits from crypto.randomBytes, return an object key not a URL, and serve via an authenticated endpoint that checks owner/admin and issues a signed URL valid for minutes (reuse lib/privateReceipts.ts). Migrate existing verification files to the private bucket and rewrite their rows. Switch all upload keys to crypto.randomUUID().
regression_test: Jest: verification upload returns no public URL; unauthenticated GET of its object returns 401/404.
